children: Snapdeal parent AceVector raises Rs 189 crore from anchor investors ahead of its Rs 420 crore IPO, which opens for subscription on 25 September
Snapdeal parent AceVector has raised Rs 189 crore from anchor investors ahead of the opening of its initial public offering on 25 September, as per a media report
The company allotted 5.91 crore shares to anchor investors at Rs 32 apiece, the upper end of its IPO price band

Two domestic mutual funds, Helios Mutual Fund and Taurus Ethical Fund, participated in the anchor round, collectively acquiring 93.75 lakh shares, or 15.87 per cent of the allocation. Helios acquired 62.48 lakh shares through two schemes, while Taurus bought 31.25 lakh shares worth Rs 10 crore

Negen Undiscovered Value Fund, a Category III AIF operated by Negen Investment Trust, was the largest anchor investor, acquiring 1.25 crore shares, or 21.16 per cent of the anchor allocation, for Rs 39.99 crore. Singularity Growth Opportunities Fund II invested Rs 26.99 crore, while TIMF Holdings acquired 15.63 lakh shares
AceVector's Rs 420 crore IPO will open for public subscription on September 25 and close on September 29. The company is expected to list on the stock exchanges on October 5
The IPO values AceVector, the parent of Snapdeal and Unicommerce, at Rs 1,741.4 crore and comprises a fresh issue of Rs 287 crore and an offer-for-sale of 4.16 crore shares
The public issue marks AceVector's second attempt to list after its earlier plans were shelved in 2022

SoftBank-backed Starfish I Pte Ltd, AceVector's largest shareholder with a 30.68 per cent stake, has reduced its proposed OFS by 34.8 per cent to 2.76 crore shares from 4.23 crore shares. Starfish I is part of AceVector's promoter group

Three Nexus-affiliated entities, Nexus India Direct Investments II, Nexus Opportunity Fund Ltd and Nexus Ventures III Ltd, will collectively sell 86.96 lakh shares, down from the 1.33 crore shares proposed earlier. Foxconn-backed FIH Business Global will sell 17.41 lakh shares

Priyanka Shreevar Kheruka, who had proposed to sell 19.37 lakh shares in the draft prospectus, will not participate in the OFS. Other selling shareholders include Jason Ashok Kothari, Rupen Investment and Industries and Centaurus Trading and Investments
AceVector plans to deploy a significant portion of the fresh IPO proceeds towards Snapdeal, its value-focused ecommerce marketplace
The company has earmarked Rs 132 crore for marketing and business promotion through FY29, including Rs 40 crore in FY27, Rs 55 crore in FY28 and Rs 37 crore in FY29

The planned spending will cover digital and social media campaigns, influencer-led promotions, product discovery and performance marketing, with a focus on expanding Snapdeal's presence among value-conscious consumers in Tier 2 and smaller cities
AceVector will also invest Rs 50 crore in Snapdeal's technology infrastructure, covering cloud computing, storage, networking, software and related technology requirements

The company plans to use the technology investment to support customer engagement and retention through personalised recommendations, improvements to the shopping experience and A/B testing. AceVector expects these requirements to increase as Snapdeal's user engagement grows and its use of AI-based capabilities expands
More than Rs 100 crore of the IPO proceeds has been earmarked for acquisitions.
